claims.text: Dynamic mechanical behavior in solidified FeNiCrMn is governed by competition between dislocation slip and deformation twinning.
Lower temperatures enhance deformation-twin activation in solidified FeNiCrMn.
Higher strain rates enhance deformation-twin activation in solidified FeNiCrMn.
Deformation twinning significantly contributes to strain hardening and ductility under low-temperature, high-strain-rate conditions.
Dislocation slip dominates in solidified FeNiCrMn at higher temperatures.
Dislocation slip dominates in solidified FeNiCrMn at lower strain rates.
Slip-dominated deformation produces less pronounced strain hardening than twin-assisted deformation.
The relevant structural mediator is the density of deformation twins and their interaction with the dislocation network.
Increased critical stress at low temperature and high strain rate promotes deformation-twin nucleation.
Interactions between deformation twins and dislocations enhance strain hardening.
Interactions between deformation twins and dislocations delay strain localization and failure.
Lower stresses at higher temperature or lower strain rate cause dislocation glide to predominate.
Low-temperature, high-strain-rate specimens will have greater twin density than high-temperature, low-strain-rate specimens.
Low-temperature, high-strain-rate specimens will exhibit enhanced strain hardening.
Low-temperature, high-strain-rate specimens will exhibit improved ductility.
At room temperature and an intermediate strain rate, dislocation motion and minimal twinning are expected to be balanced.
The proposed mechanism is limited to Co-free FeNiCrMn with a cast microstructure and may not apply after severe plastic deformation or annealing.
Post-solidification processing can alter defect structures and mechanical behavior.
Mechanical testing over approximately 10^-3 to 10 s^-1 is an appropriate strain-rate matrix for examining dynamic response.
The quantitative twinning contribution and the temperature–strain-rate transition thresholds are presently uncertain and may depend on minor composition changes.
